Milestones of Autonomous Mathematics 
April 13–17, 2026
Co-sponsored by ICARM and Principia Labs
Location: San Francisco, CA

What should the milestones of progress in mathematical AI actually look like—beyond headlines and hype? This workshop brings mathematicians together to define a concrete, multidimensional framework: roughly 8 categories of AI capability (e.g. problem solving, generalization, exposition, formalization, conjecturing, …) with graded milestones in each.

Organizing Committee: Elliot Glazer (Principia Labs), Daniel Litt (Toronto), Jacob Tsimerman (Toronto), Alex Kontorovich (Rutgers), Ravi Vakil (Stanford)

If you would like to participate, send a CV and a brief statement of interest to events@icarm.io. Limited funding is available from Principia Labs, so let us know if you need support. We may accommodate single-day or online participation if there is sufficient interest in such an option.

https://icarm.io/project/milestones-of-autonomous-mathematics/
Discussion at #general > Discussion: Milestones of Autonomous Mathematics

Participants in the Milestones for Autonomous Mathematics Research workshop have been meeting this week to discuss ways to assess the ability of AI systems to suppport mathematics research. On Thursday, April 16 and Friday, April 17, the meeting will assume an online/hybrid format.

On Thursday, from 9 am to 12 pm Pacific Time, there will be a sequence of short talks from workshop attendees presenting the state of the milestones. Thursday afternoon (1-2pm Pacific Time) will have a short presentation on the structure of the test evaluation. The rest of Thursday and Friday will have office hours to on-board people interested in the project.
